title: Filmation castle
description: Every room in a Filmation game, and the floor shapes they stand on. The editable form: rooms_source.py turns it, with templates.json beside it, into room_data.s, and the room designer opens it as a picture. A room places templates by name; the templates themselves are templates.json's.

meta.description: About the file rather than the castle. rooms_source.py ignores all of it, so nothing here changes one byte of the game.

game.description: Which game, naming a directory under examples/filmation.

comment.description: Prose for whoever opens the file.

sprites.description: Which sheet the graphic names in this file go with. The designer resolves a name through these; the paths are relative to this file, and neither host will follow one that is absolute or climbs out of the directory.

atlas.description: The atlas that names and locates each frame, normally sprites.json.

graphics.description: Which sprite each graphic number draws and the pixel nudge that lines it up, normally graphic_map.json.

templates.description: The file this castle's templates are in, beside this one. Required: nothing is assumed about where it is, and it has to name this file back in its own meta.rooms.

roomDimensions.description: The floor shapes a room can have, keyed by name. room_shape copies the three bytes into room_half_u, room_half_v and room_floor_z; the floor is centred on 128 along both axes. The key ORDER is the game's own -- bits 3 and 4 of a room's attribute byte index this table straight -- so a shape may be renamed but not moved.

z.description: The floor's height: where a piece resting on the floor sits.

rooms.description: The castle. A room is a colour, a floor shape and a handful of indices; room_build.s expands those into the records the engine draws.

number.description: The room's own number. In Knight Lore the map is arithmetic -- a 16 x 16 grid, so the number is a row and a column -- and in Pentagram each doorway carries its destination instead.

ink.description: The room's ink colour, 0 to 7. Black on black would be a room you cannot see.

dimensions.description: Which of `roomDimensions` gives this room its floor, by name.

scenery.description: The scenery templates this room is built from, in the order they are drawn.

destination.description: Pentagram only: the room a doorway leads to. Knight Lore works its own out from the room number.

objects.description: Object templates, each stamped at one or more places on the floor grid.

z.description: Which level up, 0 to 3. room_unpack turns it into 12 units a level.

nudge.description: Knight Lore only: a sixth byte nudging this one placement.

graphic.description: A sprite's name from the sheet, not a number: a path through the sprite groups, then which one it is within its group, counting from one -- knight.legs.1. A frame shared by several graphic numbers takes the number as a last segment (knight.legs.1.g144), because they are not interchangeable. A graphic with no artwork at all is gfx_NN. graphics.py is the one place names and numbers meet; rooms_source.py stops on a name it cannot place rather than emit a wrong byte.

flags.description: The game's own flag byte. Two bits are known and named; the rest are carried whole rather than guessed at.

mirrored.description: Bit 6: draw the artwork the other way round. The nudge may differ when it is -- see graphic_map.json.

passable.description: Bit 1: things walk through it rather than into it.

rest.description: The bits we have not named, kept so the file claims no more than is actually known.
